title: Vertiv advances 800 VDC power architectures to support growing AI data center demands
summary: Vertiv Holdings Co. (NYSE: VRT), a global leader in critical digital infrastructure, today added 800 VDC systems for the AI compute pod and the data hall, extending a portfolio that began with the May 2026 introduction of the Vertiv™ PowerDirect 5000 Power Rack to three deployment levels: rack, compute pod and data hall.
body_markdown:
800 VDC portfolio to be showcased at the Vertiv booth at the SC26 International Conference for High-Performance Computing, Networking, Storage, and Analysis


**COLUMBUS, Ohio (Nov. 17, 2026)** — Vertiv Holdings Co. (NYSE: VRT), a global leader in critical digital infrastructure, today added 800 VDC systems for the AI compute pod and the data hall, extending a portfolio that began with the May 2026 introduction of the Vertiv™ PowerDirect 5000 Power Rack to three deployment levels: rack, compute pod and data hall.[The expanded portfolio](https://www.vertiv.com/en-us/solutions/800-VDC-power-architectures-for-AI-data-centers/) enables operators to meet rising power demands in next-generation AI data centers and scale infrastructure as compute requirements evolve.


As AI workloads continue to increase power requirements across the data center, operators are evaluating 800 VDC as a potential path to support higher-density computing environments, but adoption will not follow a single architecture or timeline. AC and DC architectures are expected to coexist, making flexibility in power conversion, distribution and deployment essential.


Operators have different facilities, workloads, business models, risk tolerances, and investment horizons. Vertiv’s role is to help operators determine which architecture matches their needs, and its portfolio provides operators with the flexibility to introduce 800 VDC at different points in the power train, aligning deployment with facility requirements without committing an entire data center to a single architecture.


“The 800 VDC power train is not just a new power product or conversion methodology; it is a set of architectures and system designs,” said Scott Armul, Chief Product and Technology Officer at Vertiv. “Delivering it takes a comprehensive portfolio that brings together power conversion, energy storage, distribution, protection, controls and safety.”


Armul added: “To meet these evolving demands, Vertiv has built a system-level 800 VDC portfolio that gives customers the flexibility to implement 800 VDC across different data center configurations. Every layer, from the medium-voltage grid to the compute tray, is designed to work together, with safety built for DC operation.”


#### 800 VDC to the Rack


The Vertiv™ PowerDirect 3000


90 kW, 19” 800 VDC Power Shelf is a 1U DC-DC converter located inside the compute rack. The power shelf converts 800 VDC to 54 VDC for compute trays at up to 98.5% peak efficiency and supports 180% pulse power for 0.5 milliseconds.


Designed for operators adding high-density AI compute to existing facilities, this architecture moves power conversion and energy storage outside the IT rack, freeing 8 to 16 rack units for additional compute. Operators can retain existing upstream AC infrastructure, helping simplify deployment without a facility redesign. With one power rack supporting one or two IT racks, the architecture helps isolate faults and simplify maintenance. The platform supports both 800 VDC and ±400 VDC through minimal hardware configuration changes, providing flexibility as silicon partners’ voltage requirements evolve. It suits brownfield environments, retrofit scenarios and facilities running mixed AC and DC architectures.


#### 800 VDC to the AI Compute Pod


The Vertiv™ PowerDirect 9000


, 1.5 MW 800 VDC Power Center converts 480 VAC to 800 VDC for an entire row or pod. It distributes power via the Vertiv™ PowerBar Track DC busway and tap-off boxes to the Vertiv™ PowerDirect 3000, 90 kW 19” 800 VDC DC/DC Power Shelves in each rack. The system scales in 60 kW increments through 27 hot-pluggable power supply units. The Vertiv™ EnergyCore Li5 800 VDC battery cabinet connects directly to the DC bus and delivers 200 kW of continuous backup at up to 98% conversion efficiency, with up to six cabinets operating in parallel through active current sharing.


Designed for operators deploying megawatt-class AI compute at the pod level, this architecture consolidates power conversion into a single system ahead of the row, reducing component count and eliminating the need for individual power racks alongside each IT rack. It can free additional space for compute and support mixed AC and DC loads within the same facility, suiting colocation providers serving tenants with different workload types and GPU generations. Consolidating power conversion, backup and distribution gives operators coordinated power management across the pod.


#### 800 VDC to the Data Hall


The Vertiv™ PowerNexus MV SST


, 5 MW 800 VDC Solid-State Transformer converts medium-voltage AC directly to 800 VDC in a single conversion stage, feeding seamlessly into the Vertiv™ DC busway. It eliminates two to three intermediate conversion steps found in conventional power trains and provides a stable DC output with galvanic isolation. Its outdoor, liquid-cooled and containerized design reduces physical footprint while delivering up to 98% AC-to-DC efficiency and providing fault ride-through and AI power smoothing when connected to external energy storage with a DC/DC converter coupled on the 800 VDC bus. A single unit can support a 4.8 MW super pod reference architecture without chaining. Bidirectional power flow enables improved grid power quality and can provide active power support.


Designed for operators building purpose-built AI factories at campus scale, this architecture simplifies the power train from the medium-voltage connection to the rack. Moving power conversion outdoors can recover valuable indoor space for compute, while fewer conversion stages help reduce cumulative power losses. Battery communication ports coordinate with energy storage systems to manage the rapid load fluctuations of AI workloads. The containerized design also supports faster deployment and standardized replication across campuses.


#### A comprehensive 800 VDC portfolio


The Vertiv™ 800 VDC portfolio addresses the varying requirements of AI data center deployments through three differentiators:


- Architecture optionality:


A hyperscaler building a purpose-built AI factory makes different choices from a colocation provider serving multiple customers. Vertiv’s 800 VDC


architectures support 800 VDC deployment at the rack, pod or data hall level, accommodating different facility requirements, workloads and mixed AC/DC environments.
- Comprehensive portfolio:


800 VDC cannot be reduced to a sidecar, a rectifier, or a single component. Vertiv’s portfolio covers power conversion, energy storage, distribution, protection, controls and monitoring to deliver a coordinated, end-to-end system.
- Safety by design:


800 VDC needs safety practices and service procedures purpose-built for DC operating environments, not adapted from legacy AC. Vertiv 800 VDC


architectures include touch-proof busbars, high voltage isolation, midpoint grounding, ground-fault detection and arc-flash prevention, supported by Vertiv™ Services offerings developed for DC environments.


“Different operators have different requirements, whether they’re building new AI facilities, upgrading existing sites, or supporting a mix of tenants and workloads,” said Kyle Keeper, Senior Vice President of Vertiv’s Power Management Business Unit. “The Vertiv 800 VDC portfolio gives each of them an architecture that fits their needs. Whether deploying at the rack, compute pod or data hall level, customers have the optionality to choose an approach that aligns with their existing infrastructure, deployment goals and power requirements. This flexibility helps them meet today’s demands while creating a path to scale as their AI infrastructure evolves.”


Vertiv is showcasing its 800 VDC portfolio at SC26, Nov. 17-22, 2026. Pilot programs, technical validation activities, and collaborative development initiatives tailored to customers’ deployment needs are currently underway. Vertiv experts are ready to discuss these solutions and engage on next steps.


For more information on Vertiv’s end-to-end portfolio of power and thermal management, infrastructure solutions, IT systems and services for critical digital applications, visit[Vertiv.com.](https://www.vertiv.com/en-us/)


*Vertiv offers three 800 VDC architecture options, spanning medium-voltage (MV) to low-voltage (LV) AC-to-800 VDC conversion at the rack, LV AC -to-800 VDC conversion at the compute pod, and MV AC-to-800 VDC conversion at the data hall, giving operators the flexibility to integrate DC power into existing infrastructure or support purpose-built AI facilities as requirements evolve. © Vertiv*
